questions.q: Who developed Privacy by Design and its 7 Foundational Principles?
options: Ann Cavoukian, former Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario, Canada
A working group within the European Commission
The US Department of Health and Human Services
The PCAOB
questions.explain: Ann Cavoukian, while serving as Ontario's Information and Privacy Commissioner, developed Privacy by Design and its 7 Foundational Principles.

questions.q: What does the 'privacy as the default setting' principle mean?
options: Users get privacy protection automatically, without needing to take any action to request it
Privacy settings should require a paid upgrade to unlock
Default settings should maximize data collection unless a user opts out
Privacy only applies after a formal complaint is filed
questions.explain: This principle means the system is private by default — the user shouldn't have to dig through settings to get protection that should already be there.

questions.q: What does 'full functionality — positive-sum, not zero-sum' mean in Privacy by Design?
options: Privacy shouldn't require trading away functionality or security — the goal is accommodating both
A system can only be either fully functional or fully private, never both
Privacy features should be removed if they reduce performance at all
Functionality always takes priority over privacy when the two conflict
questions.explain: Privacy by Design rejects the idea that privacy must come at the cost of functionality or security; it treats accommodating both as the goal, not a zero-sum trade-off.

questions.q: How does GDPR Article 25 relate to Privacy by Design, per this lesson?
options: Article 25 requires 'data protection by design and by default,' turning this design philosophy into a binding legal requirement under GDPR
Article 25 bans the use of Privacy by Design principles in the EU
Article 25 is unrelated to Privacy by Design and covers breach notification instead
Article 25 only applies to healthcare organizations
questions.explain: GDPR Article 25 requires 'data protection by design and by default,' which operationalizes Ann Cavoukian's design philosophy directly into EU law.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is retrofitting privacy into an existing system described as expensive and incomplete?
options: Because controls are added on top of a data flow that was never built to support them, after sensitive data may already exist in unplanned places
Because retrofitting always costs exactly four times the original build cost
Because GDPR legally prohibits any system from being modified after launch
Because retrofitted systems are always less functional than new ones by law
questions.explain: The lesson explains that bolting privacy on afterward means adding controls to a system never designed for them and discovering sensitive data in unplanned places, which is harder and costlier than designing it in from the start.
